oh_midstream.blurb: Midstream is a stretch of sandstone boulders in the wooded gorge of Chippewa Creek, in Brecksville Reservation south of Cleveland. The problems here are all bouldering, running from V0 up to the V7 range, with the bulk of them in the V2 to V4 bracket. Lines range from short pinchy aretes to steeper, more powerful moves. Reaching the boulders means walking down from the gorge overlook or the playground side and following the creek, so expect some uneven dirt and rock underfoot. The sandstone turns fragile when wet, so it pays to wait several dry days after rain. Spring and fall bring the best conditions; summer is buggy near the water and winter is icy.

oh_scioto_audubon_metro_park.blurb: This is a purpose-built outdoor wall in Columbus, on the Whittier Peninsula a short walk from downtown. The structure is fiberglass, roughly 35 feet tall, made up of three towers and two arches, with room for a good number of climbers at once. Bouldering and top-rope laps make up most of what is here, with a few bolted lead lines, and grades run from easy up through V6 and into the 5.12 range. Top-rope anchors sit above the wall, reached by scrambling up the back, and some are set well back from the cable, so bring a long sling. Pads are worthwhile for the taller boulder problems, and the skyline views are a bonus.

oh_main_wall.blurb: The Main Wall is the central cliff at Whipp's Ledges in Hinckley Reservation, south of Cleveland. The rock is a quartz-rich sandstone, with faces about 20 to 50 feet tall. Most of the climbing here is top rope, with a smaller share of trad and a few boulder problems. Cracks, arêtes and faces are all on offer, and grades run from 5.5 into the 5.12 range, with plenty of climbs between 5.8 and 5.12. Bring a long static rope for natural anchors, since many setups are built from trees. The sandstone gets brittle when wet, so give it a day or two to dry after rain. A short walk from either parking area gets you there.

oh_a_night_moves_area.blurb: Night Moves is the first group of boulders you meet at Raven Rocks, a quiet, wooded gorge area in eastern Ohio. All of the climbing is bouldering, and the walk from the parking area is brief and easy, on a flat path. The boulders and roofs carry a broad spread of difficulty, with a good number of problems from V3 through V7 plus a handful of harder lines and projects, so it suits stronger boulderers more than beginners. A smaller boulder nearby works well for warming up. The access roads are unpaved and steep in spots, which makes snowy days a poor bet, and cell service is weak, so save your maps beforehand.

oh_coad_boulders.blurb: The COAD boulders sit along the south end of Copperhead Ridge on the edge of Athens, in the hills of southeast Ohio. They are among the most worthwhile bouldering in town. The rock is sandstone and every problem is a boulder, mostly in the V1 to V3 range with a few V0s and a handful of V4 and V5 lines, so the area suits climbers working through the moderates. Local sandstone is soft and damages easily when wet, and little of it dries quickly, so wait at least two dry days. Fall tends to be the most pleasant time. The nearby trails are popular with mountain bikers, and the single-track gets muddy when wet.

oh_cuyahoga_falls_glens_climbs.blurb: A riverside pocket of boulders and small cliffs in the gorge of the Cuyahoga River, right in the middle of Cuyahoga Falls. Despite the downtown setting, the gorge feels secluded and quiet. Nearly everything here is bouldering, on sandstone with a pebbly conglomerate base, and the grades are wide-ranging: lots of V0 to V4, plus a scattering of harder problems, a few up around V8 to V10. There are also a couple of top-rope and trad lines. The footing near the water is steep and loose, and a slip can mean sliding a long way down, so bring pads and a spotter.

oh_clear_creek_crag.blurb: Clear Creek Crag is the first wall you reach along the river trail on the southeast side of Mad River Gorge, an area nicknamed the Darkside, near Springfield. It is mostly bolted sport climbing with a handful of trad lines, and the difficulty leans hard: the bulk of routes fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a few 5.9s as a way in. The area is wooded and the climbs are known for being technical. From the parking lot it is a short stroll past the kiosk, down the main stairway and along the river path, which can be slick when wet. The left side of the crag draws the most traffic, so a quieter neighboring wall may be a better pick on busy days.

oh_rectangle_rock.blurb: Rectangle Rock is a bouldering area in Hocking Hills State Forest, in the hills of southeast Ohio. The rock is Blackhand sandstone, and quality is generally good for the region. Nearly all of the climbing is boulder problems, most in the V0 to V4 range with a few harder V6 and V7 lines, plus a small number of top-rope routes. There are no fixed anchors, so any top rope has to be built from scratch. The setting is open with nice views, and it is typically shaded but picks up enough sun to dry most exposed rock. Walk in across the footbridge and along the horse trail to reach the far end of the cliff.

oh_witches_front.blurb: Witches Front is a cluster of boulders and short cliff band in the woods just outside Athens, in southeast Ohio. Almost all of the climbing is bouldering, with a few sport, trad or top-rope lines mixed in. Grades start at V0 and reach about V7, but most problems sit between V1 and V4. The site is shady and heavily treed, with a highway within view, and it sees modest crowds. Tops of the boulders tend to be slopey and loose, so bring pads and a good spotter, and plan on a steep walk uphill from the road. The sandstone is soft and best avoided right after rain.
